summary: Audit of the nine Design and verification lessons and case.json against BS 7671 A3:2024 and A4:2026, 20 Oct 2026. No worked figure changes: A4 leaves the maximum Zs tables, disconnection times, Cmin and Cmax, the above-ground current tables and the voltage drop limits as they were. Lessons 1, 3, 4 and 5 need nothing. Three things matter most. Lesson 8: C7's walkway bollards are lighting the public can reach, so the circuit needs a 30 mA RCD (an RCBO), and any buried feed needs armour or an N750 duct; A2 already required the RCD and A4 sharpens it. Lesson 2: A4's 536.4.202 says outright that diversity is never a board's overload protection, so the Section B point that switchgear may be chosen on diversified demand is wrong for boards. Lesson 6: the EV answer should name the RDC-PD that A4 accepts in place of the RCD, say no AFDD is needed, and drop its "check the amendment" hedge. Smaller: lesson 7 names 434.2.1 for the motor leg, lesson 9 asks for PME or PNB, and case.json's edition line is out of date.

i2.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i2.lesson.verified.json, written.b1.points[3].text (Section B point, also in the Book)
i2.now: You can choose the supply, submains and switchgear for the demand they will really carry, not for every load at once.
i2.replace: You can choose the supply and submains for the demand they will really carry, not for every load at once. A board is different. Its rating must cover the device that feeds it, or its whole connected load taken at 100%. Otherwise load management must cap its demand.
i2.note: Add to the point's cite: "BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 Regulation 536.4.202".

i2.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i2.lesson.verified.json, written.b1.model (Section B model answer, step "Section B", also in the Book)
i2.now: It also lets you choose the supply, submains and switchgear for the demand they will really carry.
i2.replace: It also lets you choose the supply and submains for the demand they will really carry. A board's own rating is not cut by diversity. It must cover the device that feeds it, or its whole connected load, unless load management caps the demand.

i2.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i2.lesson.verified.json, summary.rule (Keep this card), after the line "Diversity figures are guidance, not a rule. Use them only where common sense allows."
i2.replace: A board is never sized by diversity. The device feeding it is no bigger than its rating, or its full connected load fits, or load management caps it.

i2.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i2.lesson.verified.json, summary.traps (Keep this card), add a sixth trap
i2.replace: {"text": "Counting on diversity to keep a board, or an RCCB inside it, from overload. The device feeding it must be no bigger than its rating, unless load management caps the demand or the full connected load fits.", "cite": "BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 Regulation 536.4.202"}

i2.now: (ends: "Then compare the heaviest phase with the supply.")
i2.replace: - Check each board against the device that feeds it. The board's rating must be at least that device's, or its full connected load must fit. Diversity sizes the supply and submains, never the board.

i6.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i6.lesson.verified.json, written.b2.points[3].text (Section B (2) point, also in the Book)
i6.now: Each charging point needs RCD protection, including protection against DC fault currents over 6 mA. That means a Type B RCD, or a Type A or F RCD with a device that detects them, unless the charger provides it.
i6.replace: Each charging point needs its own RCD of 30 mA or less, Type A, F or B. A device to BS IEC 62955 called an RDC-PD may take its place. Each point also needs protection against DC fault current of 6 mA or more. That is a Type B RCD, or a Type A or F RCD with a device that detects DC, unless the charger provides it.

i6.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i6.lesson.verified.json, written.b2.points, a new sixth point (need stays "any three")
i6.replace: {"text": "No AFDD is needed on a circuit to EV charging equipment with standard charging sockets or connectors.", "cite": "BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 Regulation 722.421.1.7.201"}

i6.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i6.lesson.verified.json, written.b2.model (step "Section B (2)", also in the Book): its last four sentences
i6.now: Each charging point needs RCD protection, including protection against DC fault currents over 6 mA. That means a Type B RCD, or a Type A or F RCD with a detecting device, unless the charger provides it. Load management can be added to bring the maximum demand down, but it is optional. Section 722 has changed in recent amendments. Check it against the amendment you work to.
i6.replace: Each charging point needs its own RCD of 30 mA or less, or an RDC-PD in its place. It also needs protection against DC fault current: a Type B RCD, or a Type A or F RCD with a device that detects DC, unless the charger provides it. No AFDD is needed on the charging circuit. Load management can be added to bring the maximum demand down, but it is optional.

i7.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i7.body.final.html, step "Section A 2(c)", the closing lines after "Its 1.5 mm² cpc holds too."
i7.now: Take the starter-to-motor leg as 3.0 m for practice. Zs at the motor is then 0.459 Ω. ... Its 1.5 mm² cpc holds too.
i7.replace: Add after it: "The 25 A breaker at DBP2 guards this smaller leg against fault current. That works because the leg can take the fault's heat. Regulation 434.2.1 sets the conditions for a device placed upstream of a step down in size."
i7.reg: 434.2.1 (redrafted in A4; new term "inherently short-circuit proof and earth fault proof")

i8.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i8.body.final.html, step "Section A 3(h)" (the AS_3H text, line 240), and the same words in steps 3(i) and 3(j) where they repeat
i8.now: A 6 A type C breaker protects it, because LED drivers draw a surge at switch-on. ... The bollards are outdoors, so a real design would pick a cable fit for that run. Here, assume the same singles run all the way.
i8.replace: A 6 A type C RCBO protects it. Type C, because LED drivers draw a surge at switch-on. An RCBO, because the walkway bollards are lighting the public can reach, so they need a 30 mA RCD unless they run on SELV. Its maximum Zs is the same 3.64 Ω, so the sums do not change. ... The bollards are outdoors. A cable buried to them needs earthed armour, or a duct strong enough to stand in for it. Here, assume the same singles run all the way, to keep the sums simple.
i8.note: A2 already required the RCD (714.411.3.4); A4 adds that "lighting" includes its wiring and control gear, and that only lighting out of reach or locked away behind IK08 counts as inaccessible. 522.8.10 note: N750 duct counts. No figure changes. In 3(i), "the breaker opens within 0.1 s" stays true of the RCBO's overcurrent part.

i8.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i8.body.final.html, the "Before you call the design done" checklist (step "What it is for", and ticked again in step 3(j))
i8.now: Every length of the run ... Breaking capacity at each device.
i8.replace: Add a line after "Breaking capacity at each device.": "Each board rated at least the device that feeds it." Ticked in 3(j) as: "DBL2 on a 10 A breaker, far inside its rating."

i8.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i8.lesson.verified.json, summary.rule (Keep this card), after "Icn ≥ the fault level at the device"
i8.replace: Lighting the public can reach: a 30 mA RCD as well, unless it is SELV.

i9.where: build/electrical/design-and-verification/i9.lesson.verified.json, written.b2.points[4].text and written.b2.model; summary.for; and i9.body.final.html step "Handing over" (the list item "The supply's characteristics.")
i9.now: The supply's characteristics, such as the declared Ze. / ... and the supply's characteristics, such as the declared Ze of 0.1 Ω.
i9.replace: Point: "The supply's characteristics: the declared Ze, and the earthing. On a TN-C-S supply, say whether it is PME or PNB." Model: "And I would give the supply's characteristics: the declared Ze of 0.1 Ω, and whether the TN-C-S supply is PME or PNB." Handing over list: "The supply's characteristics, including PME or PNB."
